subject: Vortex production: sudden 5xx/429 surge, timeouts & autoscale lag
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@vortex.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <ops@vortex.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production 5xx/429 spike — urgent

Dylan,

We're seeing a large spike in 5xx and 429 responses across our API starting ~08:45 PT. Customer complaints rolling in — timeouts and throttled requests. We are on a Redwood Dedicated pool (pool-id: vx-ded-3) with reserved capacity.

Symptoms: 
- 5xx burst (500/502) and elevated 429s not explained by client rate limits
- Many requests timing out after 30s (we've increased client timeouts to capture headers)
- Retries from our SDK look like they're amplifying the traffic (retry loops)

Sample request IDs: rids: [vx-7a3b, vx-7a4f, vx-7a9c] attached as request-ids.csv and a header dump (vortex-headers.log).

Can Redwood confirm whether this is a capacity/executor issue or infra-side? We need a point of contact and ETA for mitigation — customers are escalating to our support ops.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
SRE Lead, Vortex.ai
attachments: request-ids.csv (text/csv), vortex-headers.log (text/log)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@vortex.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production 5xx/429 spike — urgent

Samir — thank you for the heads-up and the attachments.

We're opening an incident now (INC-20270318-1) and assembling SRE/serving on the call. Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm whether any traffic changes or rollout happened on your side in the last hour?
- Attach sample full request/response payloads if available (obfuscated is fine).

Planned immediate actions from Redwood:
- Check Dedicated pool vx-ded-3 node health and queue lengths
- Look for autoscaler activity + recent failures/cooldowns
- If node saturation is confirmed, we can temporarily enable burst capacity on the pool and fail traffic to a lower-cost compatible model variant to relieve pressure.

I'll be on a quick conference at 09:40 PT to triage — proposing a 15m bridge at 09:50 PT. Monica & Aditya are on copy to coordinate the mitigation and customer comms.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production 5xx/429 spike — immediate triage steps

Team — summary from initial checks:
- Observed: node GPU utilization in vx-ded-3 at 98% across several nodes; queue length spike and long tail latencies in scheduler logs.
- Autoscaler: attempted scale-up at 08:52 but several new nodes failed health checks (OOM on init), leaving pool short during the surge.
- Retry amplification: client SDK retries are requeueing and increasing instantaneous QPS.

Immediate mitigation proposals (to act now):
1) Increase pool burst capacity (manual add + warm nodes) to clear backlog.
2) Temporarily route non-critical routes to blue fallback model (quantized variant) to reduce per-token GPU load.
3) Backoff policy: push request throttling to Vortex side for endpoints hitting low SLAs to stop amplification (obvious ask to Ops).
4) Tune serving batch size downward for the next 60m to reduce latency under pressure.

Markus — can you approve manual scale and a short batch-size override? I'll coordinate with infra to provision warm nodes.

Monica
Senior Customer Reliability Eng, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production 5xx/429 spike — approve/manual actions

I've reviewed the cluster logs. Root cause hypothesis so far: autoscaler health-check failures (init OOMs) prevented scale from honoring recent demand — pool short by ~3 nodes at peak; combined with large batches for the current model variant leading to long GC/compaction windows and subsequent 502/504s.

Approvals & actions I signed off on now:
- Manual +3 node add to vx-ded-3 (warm nodes requested, ETA ~8–10m)
- Set pool burst to allow +5 nodes for next 30m
- Apply temporary serving override: reduce max batch size by 30% for affected model route

Ask Sales/AM (Dylan/Aditya) to surface to the customer that we're doing manual scaling and a safety fallback. If customer requires SLA credits or exec-level engagement, escalate to Laura.

I'll follow the node add and post updates here.
— Markus
VP, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@vortex.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production 5xx/429 spike — urgent

Thanks for the quick triage. Two asks from our side: 
1) We need an exec contact — our Ops team is getting pressure from Product and Legal.
2) ETA on full remediation and whether this will reoccur next hour — customers are watching.

Also, please confirm whether Redwood will accept post-incident SLA credits if root cause ties to autoscale lag.

Alicia (ops) and I will join the bridge.

Samir
SRE Lead, Vortex.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@vortex.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 18:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production 5xx/429 spike — executive note & next steps

Samir & team — I'm Laura Bennett (VP, Customer Success). I'm stepping in to make sure we move from triage to remediation and that Vortex has clear next steps and timely communications.

What we've done so far:
- Manual scaling +3 nodes completed within 12m of approval; burst capacity enabled for 30m and then stepped down as load normalized.
- Batch-size override applied; in-flight queues drained and 5xx/429 rates dropped to baseline by ~12:05 PT on 3/18.
- We collected scheduler traces, node init logs, and the failing init images that led to autoscaler retries.

Next steps (we'll follow up with a full RCA & postmortem):
- Root cause analysis (Engineering) — target: preliminary RCA in 48 hours.
- Compensation: We will evaluate SLA credit per the contract (Deal VX-4521) once the RCA verifies autoscale root cause.
- Prevention: We'll propose a small pre-warm policy for dedicated pools and an autoscaler health-check hardening patch (Engineering).

I will own exec communications and the credit discussion until resolved. Expect a short incident summary from Monica tomorrow and a tracking doc (linking the postmortem template).

Apologies for the disruption — we take this seriously. We'll schedule a postmortem call and share timelines.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
